newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria to restart Forcados output.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria to restart Forcados output.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Monday it would restart normal production from Forcados after reaching agreement with local communities to reopen oil flow stations shut at the weekend.

"We got an agreement with the people last night and we are in the process of reopening two to three flow stations in Ogidigben closed at the weekend," a senior Shell official in the midwestern oil town of Warri said by telephone from there.
The official could not immediately give a figure for the amount of crude oil involved in the closure of Ogidigben.
Shell said on Friday that 20 percent of Forcados crude, roughly 95,000 barrels per day (bpd) had been shut in by closures as a result of ethnic clashes in the oil-producing Niger delta swamp lands.

Shell declared force majeure on some cargos of Forcados blend due for lifting from April 29th because of the closure of the flow stations. The battles by militant youths were over the relocation of a local council headquarters.
"The force majeure was to do with Ogidigben and I imagine that when we reopen the flow stations there we should be back in business," he said.
The Warri official said Warri River flow station, which was closed more than a week ago because of the communal crisis, was not among the facilities being reopened.
"Warri River is still closed with the loss of 2,000 bpd," he said.
Scores of lives have been lost in the conflict in Warri while Shell, the biggest oil operator in Nigeria has been forced to close several oil flow stations and to evacuate staff.
The semi-official Daily Times newspaper on Monday quoted a top military comander as saying the authorities would act decisively to end the crisis in Warri.
"We have had enough of this," Major-General Felix Mujakperuo, general officer comanding the 82 division of the army said in Warri when he visited the area at the weekend.
Oil accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange income and last week the army deployed troops into Warri to stop the fighting.
